data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"An idempotent operation satisfies f(f(x))=f(x): repeated application yields the same result as a single application. A safe operation merely guarantees no harmful side effects on retry but may produce non-identical observable states (e.g., duplicate entries). An append-only event log with at-least-once delivery must require idempotent writers because deterministic replay demands that the final log content be identical regardless of how many delivery retries occurred; safety alone permits benign duplicates that break replay determinism.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the log infrastructure itself enforces deduplication independent of writer-supplied keys (e.g., via content-addressed storage), then safety alone may suffice and idempotency need not be required of writers.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'safe' is defined to include 'no observable state change on retry' (a stronger definition than merely 'no harm'), then safe and idempotent collapse for this purpose.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log's replay mechanism tolerates duplicate entries (e.g., by replaying with downstream deduplication), then idempotent writers are unnecessary and safe writers suffice.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In at-least-once delivery, a writer's append may be executed multiple times. If the writer is only 'safe,' each retry appends a new entry, and the log's content varies with retry count, violating deterministic replay. If the writer is idempotent\u2014e.g., by including a content hash or operation ID that the log uses to deduplicate\u2014repeated appends collapse to a single entry, preserving determinism. The idempotency requirement is on the writer's submitted operation (including its deduplication key), not on the bare append primitive.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
